### Module(s)

mini.operators

### Description

Joining a single line is simple with `J`. However, joining multiple lines is tricky as it requires visual mode (ex: Joining a paragraph would be `vipJ`).

I think the `gJ` operator would solve that (and make the whole thing `dot` repeatable). The example above of joining an inner-paragraph would be `gJip`.

Here is what I currently have in my config. However, I would probably be in a better place here rather than in a random dude's dotfiles:

```lua
local M = {}

-- Helper function to join lines in a range
local function join_lines(start_line, end_line)
  if start_line >= end_line then
    return false
  end

  -- Save cursor position
  local cursor_pos = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)

  -- Move to start line
  vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, {start_line, 0})

  -- Join lines from start to end
  local lines_to_join = end_line - start_line
  for i = 1, lines_to_join do
    vim.cmd("normal! J")
  end

  -- Restore cursor position (adjust for joined lines)
  local new_row = math.min(cursor_pos[1], start_line)
  vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, {new_row, cursor_pos[2]})

  return true
end

-- Main gJ operator function
function M.gj_operator(motion_type)
  local start_pos = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, "[")
  local end_pos = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, "]")

  local start_line = start_pos[1]
  local end_line = end_pos[1]

  -- Do nothing if the selection is within a single line
  if start_line == end_line then
    return
  end

  -- Join the lines
  local success = join_lines(start_line, end_line)

  -- Set up for dot repeat if successful
  if success then
    vim.o.operatorfunc = "v:lua.require'core.operators'.gj_operator"
  end
end

-- Setup function to create the gJ operator
function M.setup()
  -- Create the gJ operator mapping
  vim.keymap.set("n", "gJ", function()
    vim.o.operatorfunc = "v:lua.require'core.operators'.gj_operator"
    return "g@"
  end, { expr = true, desc = "Join lines with motion" })

  -- Also support visual mode
  vim.keymap.set("x", "gJ", function()
    local start_pos = vim.fn.getpos("'<")
    local end_pos = vim.fn.getpos("'>")

    local start_line = start_pos[2]
    local end_line = end_pos[2]

    -- Do nothing if selection is within a single line
    if start_line == end_line then
      return
    end

    -- Exit visual mode and join lines
    vim.cmd("normal! \27") -- Escape to exit visual mode
    join_lines(start_line, end_line)
  end, { desc = "Join selected lines" })
end

return M
```

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

As there is `:h :join` command, I think it is fairly straightforward to have this implemented manually:

```lua
_G.join_operatorfunc = function() vim.cmd("'[,']join") end
vim.keymap.set('n', 'gJ', function()
  vim.o.operatorfunc = 'v:lua.join_operatorfunc'
  return 'g@'
end, { expr = true })
vim.keymap.set('x', 'gJ', ':join<CR>')
```

Closing as not planned.
